questions.question: The enzymes integrase, protease and reverse transcriptase are found in which virus?
questions.explanation:
When the virus invades a CD4 cell, the cell becomes reprogrammed to create new copies of HIV. To
do this, HIV needs the help of certain enzymes: reverse transcriptase, protease, and integrase.

questions.question: What does the term bacteriophage refer to?
questions.explanation:
A bacteriophage is a type of virus that infects bacteria. The term phage means to devour. (bacteria
eater)
options: A. A virus that infects bacteria
B. A bacterium that infects virus
C. A virus which behaves as bacteria
questions.correct_answer: A. A virus that infects bacteria

questions.question: What of the following virus contains single stranded DNA?
questions.explanation:
Single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) viruses are widespread in the environment and include economically,
medically, and ecologically important pathogens. Parvovirus is a single stranded DNA virus which
causes disease in rats.

questions.question: How may tail fibrils are attached to the end plate of a bacteriophage?
questions.explanation:
The phage tail is a complex, multiprotein structure that mediates attachment, digestion and
penetration of the cell wall and genome ejection. There are six short tail fibers (STFs) folded beneath
the baseplate that unfold upon host recognition.

questions.question: Each carrier in Electron Transport Chain is first _________ and then _________. 2 The 3 main steps of the electron transport chain?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Generating a Proton Motive Force.
Step 2: ATP Synthesis via Chemiosmosis.
Step 3: Reduction of Oxygen.

questions.question: Electron transport chain explains:
questions.explanation:
The electron transport chain is a series of four protein complexes that couple redox reactions,
creating an electrochemical gradient that leads to the creation of ATP in a complete system
named oxidative phosphorylation

questions.question: What is the colour of Chlorophyll-b molecule?
questions.explanation:
Chlorophyll a is blue-green, chlorophyll b is yellow-green, carotene appears bright yellow, and
xanthophyll is pale yellow green.

questions.question: Upon initial hydrolysis starch yields:
questions.explanation:
On partial hydrolysis of starch and glycogen, We can obtain the disaccharide maltose and a low
molecular weight dextran.

questions.question: Human Bone cells contain ……… % of water?
questions.explanation:
The organs with the lowest percentage of water in the human body are the teeth (8%) and bones
(20-25%)

questions.question: Unique three-dimensional shape of the fully folded polypeptide, constitutes:
questions.explanation:
The overall three-dimensional structure of a polypeptide is called its tertiary structure. The tertiary
structure is primarily due to interactions between the R groups of the amino acids that make
up the protein.
3

questions.question: Butyric acid is a ________ carbon fatty acid.
questions.explanation: Butyric Acid is a saturated short-chain fatty acid with a 4-carbon backbone.

questions.question: Which of the following is a conjugated molecule?
questions.explanation:
A compound formed by chemically joining two or more different substances. Examples of
conjugated proteins are phosphoproteins, glycoproteins, nucleoproteins, chromoproteins,
lipoproteins, flavoproteins, metalloproteins

questions.question: Hydrolysis process is a reverse of -------------- process.
questions.explanation:
Condensation is a chemical reaction that involves the synthesis of a complex molecule from small
reactant molecules. Hydrolysis: Hydrolysis is the breakdown of a large reactant molecule into
small fragments in the presence of water.

questions.question: Proteins are the main ----------- of the cell?
questions.explanation:
most of the structure in a cell are made of proteins. Proteins are the main structural components of
cell

questions.question: Cell wall may be absent in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that lack a cell wall and surrounded by their cell membrane only.

questions.question: Which of the following are single membranous organelles?
questions.explanation:
There are four types of single-membrane-bound organelles: Golgi bodies, the ER , vacuole
/lysosomes , and peroxisomes
options: C. Golgi bodies, Lysosome and ER
D. Golgi bodies, lysosome and mitochondria
questions.correct_answer: C. Golgi bodies, Lysosome and ER

questions.question: Movement of molecules against the concentration gradient is?
questions.explanation:
Active transport is the transport of molecules that require the use of energy, in the form of an
energy-storing chemical called ATP (adenosine triphosphate) to help them cross the cell
membrane.

questions.question: The digestive vacuoles and autophagosomes are also known as?
questions.explanation:
The digestive vacuoles and autophagosomes are also known as Secondary Lysosomes. They are also
involved in the autophagy (self-eating). During this process some old, worn out parts of cell,
such as old mitochondria are digested

questions.question: The cell wall of Bacteria is made up of:
questions.explanation:
The cell wall consists mainly of peptidoglycan (PG), a mesh of polysaccharide strands. Peptidoglycan
is also known as murein.

questions.question: Which one is common in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation:
Ribosomes are the cellular organelles that carry out protein synthesis. They are found in both
prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

questions.question: There is no clear difference between dendrites and axons in sensory neurons, except:
The neurotransmitter active outside the CNS (Central Nervous System) is:
questions.explanation:
Acetylcholine. This excitatory neurotransmitter does a number of functions in your central nervous
system (CNS [brain and spinal cord]) and in your peripheral nervous system (nerves that
branch from the CNS)

questions.question: Hormone produced by placenta is:
questions.explanation:
Progesterone helps to prepare the body for pregnancy by stimulating glandular development and
the development of new blood vessels. This provides a good environment for implantation by
a fertilized egg.

questions.question: The middle layer of meninges is:
questions.explanation:
6
Three layers of membranes known as meninges protect the brain and spinal cord. The delicate
inner layer is the pia mater. The middle layer is the arachnoid, a web-like structure filled with
fluid that cushions the brain. The tough outer layer is called the dura mater.

questions.question: The part of brain which guides smooth and accurate motions and maintains body position is:
questions.explanation:
The cerebellum is located in the back of your brain. It helps with the coordination and movement
related to motor skills, especially involving the hands and feet. It also helps maintain posture,
balance, and equilibrium.

questions.question: Water vascular system or ambulacral system is a unique and complex system specially present in?
questions.explanation:
Echinoderms possess a unique ambulacral or water vascular system, consisting of a central ring
canal and radial canals that extend along each arm. Water circulates through these structures
and facilitates gaseous exchange as well as nutrition, predation, and locomotion.

questions.question: Round worms belong to which phylum?
questions.explanation:
Roundworms: Phylum Nematoda. Species in the phylum Nematoda (from the Greek root word
nema meaning thread) are better known as the roundworms

questions.question: Silver fish is a/an?
questions.explanation:
Silverfish are small insects that can infest a home. Although they are not dangerous, they can
damage property and trigger allergies.

questions.question: Enzymes lower the activation energy by stabilizing the transition state of a metabolic reaction due to?
questions.explanation:
By binding substrates to their active sites, enzymes stabilize the structure of the transition state.
This in turn lowers of the free energy of the transition state.
options: A. Changing conditions within the active site
B. Changing conditions within the protein framework
C. Rearranging the fatty acids in active site
D. Distorting the molecules in the allosteric site
questions.correct_answer: A. Changing conditions within the active site

questions.question: Competitive inhibitors compete with?
questions.explanation:
A competitive inhibitor competes with substrate for binding to an active site. When the inhibitor
occupies the active site, it forms an enzyme-inhibitor complex and the enzyme cannot react
until the inhibitor dissociates.

questions.question: Non-competitive inhibitor molecules have:
questions.explanation:
In noncompetitive inhibition, the inhibitor binds at an allosteric site separate from the active site of
substrate binding. Thus in noncompetitive inhibition, the inhibitor can bind its target enzyme
regardless of the presence of a bound substrate.
options: A. A similar structure to the normal substrate molecule
B. A quite different structure from the substrate molecule
C. A different conformation but fit into the active site
D. A similar conformation but does not fit into the active site
questions.correct_answer: B. A quite different structure from the substrate molecule

questions.question: What is the best physiological pH for optimum functioning for most of the cellular enzymes of human?
questions.explanation:
8
An enzyme has an optimum pH. Although most enzymes remain high activity in the pH range
between 6 and 8, some specific enzymes work well only in extremely acidic (pH <5.0) or alkaline
(pH >9.0) conditions.

questions.question: For evolutionary process to occur, which of the following is NOT a geographical barrier?
questions.explanation:
Geographic barriers include the formation of a mountain range, the movement of a glacier, and the
division of a large lake into several smaller lakes.

questions.question: According to the Biogenetic Law of Ernst Haeckel:
questions.explanation:
Biogenetic law, also called Recapitulation Theory, postulation, by Ernst Haeckel in 1866, states that
ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny (the development of the animal embryo and young traces the
evolutionary development of the species)
options: A. There is survival of the fittest
B. There is use and disuse of organs

questions.question: The animal species on Galapagos resemble species living on the:
questions.explanation:
On the Galapagos Islands, Charles Darwin observed that tortoises resembled those found in South
America.
Three extant species of Geochelone exist on mainland South America and are therefore the best
candidates for the closest living relative of the Galápagos tortoises: Geochelone denticulata, the
South American yellow-footed tortoise; Geochelone carbonaria, the South American red-footed
tortoise; and Geochelone chilensis, the Chaco tortoise.

questions.question: Digested food from intestine is carried to the liver by?
questions.explanation:
9
The hepatic portal vein is the part of the hepatic portal system. It carries blood from the intestines,
gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen and delivers it to the liver. It contains blood with nutrients
and toxins after digestion.

questions.question: -------- proteins are produced by WBCs in response to -------- and provide immunity?
questions.explanation:
Antibodies are produced by B cells (specialized white blood cells). When an antigen encounters
a B cell, it causes the B cell to divide and clone. These cloned B cells — or plasma cells —
release millions of antibodies into your bloodstream and lymph system.

questions.question: The lymphatic vessels of the body empty the lymph into blood stream at?
questions.explanation:
Lymphatic vessels empty the lymph into the right lymphatic duct and left lymphatic duct (also
called the thoracic duct). These ducts connect to the subclavian vein, which returns lymph to
your bloodstream. The subclavian vein runs below your collarbone.

questions.question: Flow of blood in the capillaries is adjusted by?
questions.explanation:
Blood flow through the capillary beds is controlled by precapillary sphincters to increase and
decrease flow depending on the body's needs and is directed by nerve and hormone signals.
Lymph vessels take fluid that has leaked out of the blood to the lymph nodes where it is
cleaned before returning to the heart.

questions.question: The pressure exerted by a solution separated by a semipermeable membrane from pure water is ________?
questions.explanation:
Osmotic pressure is the minimum pressure which needs to be applied to a solution to prevent the
inward flow of its pure solvent across a semipermeable membrane. It is also defined as the
measure of the tendency of a solution to take in its pure solvent by osmosis.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of anaerobic respiration in humans muscles cells?
questions.explanation:
10
Anaerobic respiration happens in muscles during hard exercise. Glucose is not completely broken
down, so less energy is released than during aerobic respiration. There is a build-up of lactic
acid in the muscles during vigorous exercise. This build up causes cramps, and pain in muscles.

questions.question: The respiratory surfaces exhibit following characteristic?
questions.explanation:
The surface must be permeable to allow gases to pass through. Furthermore, having an extensive
blood supply is vital, in the case of alveoli the capillary network ensures that oxygen rich blood
can be transported away from the lungs.
options: B. It must be thick for low diffusion
D. It should have low ventilation mechanism

questions.question: Which of the following is a prokaryote?
questions.explanation:
Prokaryotes are organisms whose cells lack a nucleus and other organelles. Prokaryotes are divided
into two distinct groups: the bacteria and the archaea. Bacteria are examples of the
prokaryotic cell type. An example is E. coli.

questions.question: Number of layers present in Gram-negative bacterial cell wall:
questions.explanation:
Gram-negative bacteria are surrounded by a thin peptidoglycan cell wall, which itself is surrounded
by an outer membrane containing lipopolysaccharide.

questions.question: The division of cocci in three planes form Sarcina, which is a cube of ---------- Cocci?
questions.explanation:
Sarcinae is a type of cocci that are arranged in a cuboidal manner, as the cells are formed by regular
cell divisions in three planes. Cocci that divide in three planes and remain in groups cube like
groups of eight.

questions.question: Nitrifying bacteria are the examples of:
questions.explanation:
Chemosynthetic bacteria include a group of autotrophic bacteria that use chemical energy to
produce their own food. Nitrobacter is chemosynthetic bacteria.

questions.question: Each human testis is divided into:
questions.explanation:
The tunica albuginea has extensions into each testis that act as partial partitions to divide the testis
into approximately 250 -290 compartments, or lobules. Each lobule contains one or more
convoluted tubules, or narrow tubes, where sperm are formed.

questions.question: Which cells in the human males are responsible for the release of testosterone?
questions.explanation:
Leydig cells produce testosterone in the testes under the pulsatile control of pituitary luteinizing
hormone
options: D. Leydig cells or interstitial cells
questions.correct_answer: D. Leydig cells or interstitial cells

questions.question: Fertilized ovum is implanted and undergoes further development in the:
questions.explanation:
Once fertilization takes, the zygote will generally travel to the uterine cavity and implant in the wall
of the uterus near the fundus.

questions.question: Level of luteinizing hormone (LH) is maximum in blood during which stage of menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation:
The ovulatory phase begins with a surge in luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone
levels. Luteinizing hormone stimulates egg release (ovulation).

questions.question: Major source of transmission of syphilis is:
questions.explanation: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI).

questions.question: What is FALSE about cartilage?
questions.explanation:
Cartilage is a strong, flexible connective tissue that protects your joints and bones. It acts as a shock
absorber throughout your body. Cartilage, once synthesized, lacks lymphatic or blood supply
and the movement of waste and nutrition is chiefly via diffusion to and from adjacent tissues.
options: A. There are many blood vessels in cartilage
B. It is a form of connective tissue
C. It covers ends of the bones at joints
D. It is much softer than bone
questions.correct_answer: A. There are many blood vessels in cartilage

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT found in skeletal muscle fibers in human?
questions.explanation:
Hemoglobin is defined as an oxygen-carrying pigment and predominant protein present in red
blood cells. It is an iron containing protein in the blood, which transports oxygen to tissues.
Myoglobin is defined as a red protein containing haem, which carries and stores oxygen in
muscle cells. It is an oxygen-binding protein, located primarily in muscle cells. Myoglobin has
more affinity to oxygen from hemoglobin. So, it is able to remove oxygen from hemoglobin.

questions.question: Hinge joint is present between which of the following bones?
questions.explanation:
Common hinge joints are knee and elbow joints. So hinge joint is present between the humerus and
ulna.

questions.question: Test cross is made to check the genotype of a trait. Which of the following crosses is a test cross?
questions.explanation:
A test cross is a way to explore the genotype of an organism. Early use of the test cross was as an
experimental mating test used to determine what alleles are present in the genotype. In its
simplest form, a test cross is an experimental cross of an individual organism of dominant
phenotype but unknown genotype and an organism with a homozygous recessive genotype
(and phenotype).

questions.question: What happens when a Rh –ve woman, married to a Rh +ve man conceives a child who is Rh +ve?
questions.explanation:
Rh incompatibility occurs when the mother's blood type is Rh negative and her fetus' blood type is
Rh positive. Antibodies from an Rh negative mother may enter the blood stream of her unborn
Rh positive infant, damaging the red blood cells (RBCs).

questions.question: DNA stores biological information in discrete units termed as:
questions.explanation:
A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Genes are made up of DNA. Some genes
act as instructions to make molecules called proteins.

questions.question: To study sex linkages in Drosophila, Morgan mated white eyed males with wild type red eyed females. What will be the phenotype of offspring?
questions.explanation:
The eye color gene is linked with to sex and is present on the X-chromosome. X-chromosome
doesn't pass directly from father to the offspring’of the same sex but follows a crisscross
inheritance, which is transferred from one sex to the offspring of the opposite sex. Since the
trait of white eye color is recessive and linked to sex, it shows its effect in the male because of
single X-chromosome. The female flies can show white-eye trait when both its X-chromosome
carry the recessive allele of the white eye. At last, Morgan concluded that only X chromosome
carries the gene for eye color in Drosophila. Y-chromosome did not have the gene for eye
color. The genes like the eye color present on the sex chromosome are said to be sex-linked or
X-linked.
options: A. All red eyed males and females
B. Red eyed females and white eyed males
C. White eyed females and red eyed males
D. All white eyed females and males
questions.correct_answer: A. All red eyed males and females

questions.question: Which one of the following is X Linked Dominant disorder?
questions.explanation:
Hereditary hypophosphatemia rickets can have several patterns of inheritance. When the condition
results from mutations in the PHEX gene, it is inherited in an X-linked dominant pattern. The
PHEX gene is located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes

homogeneous catalyst. In these reactions, the catalyst, reactant, and products are in the same

questions.question: Which of the following compound is more acidic?
questions.explanation:
A hydrogen tends to be more acidic when attached to a more electronegative atom. Alkynes are
more acidic than alkenes, which are in turn more acidic than alkanes, because sp carbon atoms
are more electronegative than sp 2 carbon atoms, which are in turn more electronegative than
sp 3 carbon atoms. cycloalkane has no electron delocalization, and thus is a much weaker acid.

questions.question: Consider the chlorination of methane, the attack of chlorine free radical on methane form methyl free radical occurs in?
questions.explanation:
The over-all process is known as free radical substitution, or as a free radical chain reaction.
1) Chain initiation: The chain is initiated (started) by UV light breaking a chlorine molecule into free
radicals
Cl2→2Cl.
2) Chain propagation reactions: These are the reactions which keeps the chain going.
CH4+Cl.→CH.3+HCl
CH.3+Cl2→CH3Cl+Cl.
3) Chain termination reactions: These are reactions which remove free radicals from the system
without replacing them by new ones
2Cl.→Cl2
CH.3+Cl.→CH3Cl
CH.3+CH.3→CH3CH3

questions.question: Which of the following is also called silver mirror test?
questions.explanation:
Tollens’ test, also known as silver-mirror test, is a qualitative laboratory test used to
distinguish between an aldehyde and a ketone. It exploits the fact that aldehydes are readily
oxidized, whereas ketones are not. Tollens’ test uses a reagent known as Tollens’ reagent,
which is a colorless, basic, aqueous solution containing silver ions coordinated to ammonia.

questions.question: When carboxylic acids and dicarboxylic acids have similar molecular weights, how do their melting points compare?
questions.explanation:
Dicarboxylic acids are solids at room temperature and they have melting points that are higher than
those of monocarboxylic acids containing the same number of carbon atoms, since stronger
associations between molecules exist, mainly as a result of hydrogen bond formation.
options: A. Carboxylic acids have greater melting points
B. Both acids have similar melting points
C. Dicarboxylic acids have greater melting points
D. No any consistent trends exits
questions.correct_answer: C. Dicarboxylic acids have greater melting points
